title: Desktop kits on Windows: gate
summary: The gate on Windows, drawn as a labelled fixture of DJDL in both presets: Welcome at the default, narrow, short and large window, inline license activation, Finish in your browser (no QR) and the device limit's browser hand-off, plus the one line the integrator writes.
compare: The product is the hero: DJDL's icon leads every step, its accent comes from the icon (kits are not service-accented), no Polaris Key mark appears, and the name is said once (the title).

DL1 on a window: two panes from 560px of window, a one-line strip below; the end pane is top-aligned; the short landscape window drops the lede and links instead of scrolling; the large window is one capped card on a flat ground.

Under polaris-key the start pane is the product art and the head carries the icon; under native it is the icon alone on the quiet ground and the head carries none, with the host's tint, fields and button style.
Inline is the default presentation (D-79) for activation and sign-in; the dialog form is the labelled alternative and is not drawn.
No QR on a desktop surface (DL14): the browser hand-off shows the code, Copy, the countdown and Open browser again with the external-action glyph.
DL6: the device limit on the key path is a neutral callout under the heading, and its fix is the one primary, Open in browser, with the external-action glyph (the key path has no in-app removal).
One primary per state; the key middle-elides at rest and its end is visible; weights 400/500/600; hairlines only; no static accent line under the title bar.
The host draws the window chrome (dots, caption buttons or header bar); the kit draws none.
Windows: the primary first, controls at 32px and 4px radius, 14px body, Fluent field under native.
